title: The SQL types at the boundary

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens when code calls `getHours()` on a `java.sql.Date`?

options.text: It returns 0, because the class zeroes the time of day
options.says: The page says java.sql.Date throws from its time-related methods rather than answering them.

options.text: It throws IllegalArgumentException, because it has no time
options.says: The page says java.sql.Date extends java.util.Date but throws IllegalArgumentException from time-related methods.

options.text: It returns the hour of its moment in the default zone
options.says: Reading the hour in the default zone is what the parent java.util.Date does; the page says java.sql.Date throws instead.

questions.stem: Per this page, with a JDBC 4.2 driver, `preparedStatement.setObject(1, localDateTime)` writes to which kind of column?

options.says: The page pairs a DATE column with setObject(1, localDate), not with a LocalDateTime.

options.text: A TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE column
options.says: The page pairs TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE with setObject(1, offsetDateTime), not with a LocalDateTime.
The page's JDBC answer writes a LocalDateTime with setObject to a TIMESTAMP column.
